title: "Aggregate subgroup information for the relaxed model"

The relaxed model gives the index and comparator treatments separate
covariate coefficients. The IPD identify `beta_index`; the comparator
coefficients are informed only through the aggregate likelihood, so what they
can be pinned down to depends on how many aggregate rows there are and how
those rows are laid out. This vignette shows what `check_identification()`
measures, how to read it, and what a simulation says about designs that pass
the row count and still fail.

## What an aggregate row contributes

For the binomial, normal and Poisson families each mutually exclusive
aggregate stratum contributes one scalar outcome summary. With $K$ covariates
the relaxed comparator model has $K + 1$ coefficients, so $S \geq K + 1$ rows
are necessary. They are not sufficient. For a normal identity-link model
stratum $s$ has mean $\bar y_s = \mu_c + m_s^\mathsf{T}\beta_c$, where $m_s$
is the declared covariate-mean vector, and the coefficients are separated only
when the design $[\mathbf{1}, M]$ has full column rank: after centering, the
mean vectors must span all $K$ covariate directions. For a nonlinear mean
model each row contributes
$\mathbb{E}_{X\sim f_s}[g^{-1}(\mu_c+X^\mathsf{T}\beta_c)]$, which depends on
the whole within-stratum distribution $f_s$, so the mean-profile geometry is
descriptive there and `check_identification()` returns `flagged = NA` once
the row count is adequate [@Phillippo2020; @ChandlerIshakMLUMR].

Multiple `set_agd()` rows are taken to be mutually exclusive, collectively
exhaustive strata of one comparator population, combined with `outcome_n` or
person-time weights; they are not overlapping subgroup analyses. If Poisson
exposure varies with the covariates, the covariate summaries must match the
person-time distribution [@RemiroAzocar2022].

## Mean-profile geometry

`check_identification()` centers the declared subgroup means, divides each
covariate by its IPD SD, and takes the singular values. `cond_inv`, the
smallest over the largest, goes to zero as the rows collapse onto a
lower-dimensional set; `spread`, the RMS distance of the rows from their
center along the dominant direction, says whether they move at all.


``` r
library(mlumr)
```

One continuous and two binary covariates. The designs below all have several
rows but span different directions.


``` r
ref_sd <- c(age = 1, sex = 0.5, prior = 0.49)

by_age_only <- cbind(age = seq(-1.5, 1.5, length.out = 6), sex = 0.5, prior = 0.4)
cross_tab <- rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(0, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 1), c(0, 1, 1))
jointly_defined <- rbind(c(-1, 0, 0), c(-1, 1, 0), c(-1, 0, 1), c(-1, 1, 1),
                         c(1, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 1))

geometry <- function(M) {
  M <- scale(as.matrix(M), center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  M <- sweep(M, 2, ref_sd, "/")
  d <- svd(M)$d
  c(rows = nrow(M), cond_inv = round(min(d) / max(d), 3),
    spread = round(max(d) / sqrt(nrow(M)), 3))
}
rbind(by_age_only = geometry(by_age_only), cross_tab = geometry(cross_tab),
      jointly_defined = geometry(jointly_defined))
#>                 rows cond_inv spread
#> by_age_only        6    0.000  1.025
#> cross_tab          4    0.000  1.020
#> jointly_defined    6    0.707  1.167
```

Age bands vary only in the age direction and the cross-tab holds age fixed;
only the jointly defined cells span all three covariates. More rows along an
existing direction cannot replace a missing one.

## Using `check_identification()`

The screen uses the declared AgD means, so it can be run before
`add_integration()`.


``` r
set.seed(2026)
n_ipd <- 120
ipd_df <- data.frame(
  trt = "A",
  y = rnorm(n_ipd, 2, 1),
  age = rnorm(n_ipd),
  sex = rbinom(n_ipd, 1, 0.5),
  prior = rbinom(n_ipd, 1, 0.4)
)
ipd <- set_ipd(ipd_df, treatment = "trt", outcome = "y",
               covariates = c("age", "sex", "prior"), family = "normal")

make_design <- function(M) {
  agd_df <- data.frame(
    trt = "B",
    n = rep(100, nrow(M)),
    ybar = 2 + 0.1 * M[, 1] + 0.2 * M[, 2] - 0.1 * M[, 3],
    yse = rep(0.1, nrow(M)),
    age_mean = M[, 1],
    age_sd = rep(1, nrow(M)),
    sex_mean = M[, 2],
    prior_mean = M[, 3]
  )
  agd <- set_agd(
    agd_df, treatment = "trt", family = "normal",
    outcome_mean = "ybar", outcome_se = "yse", outcome_n = "n",
    cov_means = c("age_mean", "sex_mean", "prior_mean"),
    cov_sds = c("age_sd", NA, NA),
    cov_types = c("continuous", "binary", "binary")
  )
  combine_data(ipd, agd)
}

identity_age <- check_identification(
  make_design(by_age_only), link = "identity", verbose = FALSE
)
identity_joint <- check_identification(
  make_design(jointly_defined), link = "identity", verbose = FALSE
)
nonlinear_joint <- check_identification(
  make_design(jointly_defined), link = "log", verbose = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  design = c("age only", "joint identity", "joint log"),
  scope = c(identity_age$diagnostic_scope,
            identity_joint$diagnostic_scope,
            nonlinear_joint$diagnostic_scope),
  rows = c(identity_age$n_rows, identity_joint$n_rows,
           nonlinear_joint$n_rows),
  cond_inv = c(identity_age$cond_inv, identity_joint$cond_inv,
               nonlinear_joint$cond_inv),
  spread = c(identity_age$spread, identity_joint$spread,
             nonlinear_joint$spread),
  flagged = c(identity_age$flagged, identity_joint$flagged,
              nonlinear_joint$flagged)
)
#>           design       scope rows     cond_inv   spread flagged
#> 1       age only    identity    6 1.487234e-33 1.075721    TRUE
#> 2 joint identity    identity    6 7.070856e-01 1.153110   FALSE
#> 3      joint log descriptive    6 7.070856e-01 1.153110      NA
```

The thresholds `cond_inv < 0.2` and `spread < 0.05` IPD SD are package
heuristics for the identity-link design, not validated cutoffs. Neither
statistic sees subgroup sample sizes, outcome precision or link curvature, so
a value above the threshold does not prove identification.

## Recommended workflow

1. Check that the rows are mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive strata
   of the comparator population, with sample sizes or exposures.
2. Count the rows against $K + 1$.
3. For a normal identity-link model read `cond_inv` and `spread`; when the
   design is deficient, request jointly defined cells that vary across all
   covariates.
4. For a nonlinear model treat the geometry as descriptive and read the
   fitted coefficient posterior, the sampler diagnostics and
   `prior_sensitivity()`.
5. Run `check_integration()` separately; numerical fidelity of the grid and
   identification are different questions.
6. Check overlap before transporting the comparator regression to another
   population [@TSD18; @ChandlerIshakTransport].

## Distribution and dependence assumptions

Each nonlinear aggregate likelihood integrates over a reconstructed
within-stratum covariate distribution, which means, SDs and a copula do not
uniquely determine, and the same correlation matrix is reused for every row.
These are sensitivity assumptions, not something a row count repairs: vary
plausible marginals and dependence structures when the estimand is sensitive
to them.

## Time-to-event outcomes

A comparator curve from `set_agd_surv()` contributes event and censoring
terms across time, not one scalar summary per row, so the counting argument
does not apply and `check_identification()` refuses survival data. For a
relaxed survival fit inspect the comparator coefficient posterior, run
`prior_sensitivity()` with `prior_beta_comparator_scales`, and compare
`aux_by = ".study"` with `aux_by = "none"` where that is defensible.

## Simulation evidence



Six aggregate designs are crossed with the three non-survival families and
300 replications each, 5400 fits in total, by the development
script
[`data-raw/simulate_subgroup_identification.R`](https://github.com/choxos/mlumr/blob/main/data-raw/simulate_subgroup_identification.R).
The numbers below come from a results file with MD5 4dc62e120a5b2ad21733c13d843ef9ec, which a test
compares against the file in the repository. Every design is a tabulation of
the same people: each replication draws one comparator cohort and reports it
six ways (age bands, a cross-tab of the two binary covariates, and designs
that cut across all three), so designs are compared within a replication as
paired contrasts. Width and coverage are summarized over fits that met every
diagnostic (split-Rhat at most 1.01, bulk and tail effective sample size at
least 400, no divergent transitions, no treedepth saturation, every chain
finished); the rest are counted separately. Coverage is scored against the
estimand the package reports, recomputed on each replication's own
covariates.

`cond_inv` is the geometry of the design as requested, evaluated at the
population profiles; `Fitted` is the same statistic on the rows the likelihood
received. Three designs (`ovat_age_3`, `ovat_age_6` and `crosstab_4`) fall
below 0.001 because their profiles span fewer than three
directions; the other three sit above 0.5. Sampling noise repays part of the
missing direction in the fitted rows, but the two groups never overlap.

Each row is that design minus the four-row `minimal_4`, over the replications
where both converged; a positive difference is a wider interval.



Three things follow.

**Row count does not order the designs; geometry does.** The six-row
one-variable-at-a-time design has more rows than the four-row minimal design
and gives a wider interval in every family. A reader counting rows would
prefer the worse design.

**An unidentified design is unpredictable, not merely imprecise.** The
coefficient of variation of the width separates the two groups completely:
every identified cell is at or below 0.05 and every
deficient one at or above 0.16. Coverage shows none
of this, because a wide enough interval covers almost anything.

**The screen is exact under the identity link and silent elsewhere.** Across
the 1800 normal fits `check_identification()`
flagged exactly the deficient designs. Under the logit and log links it
withholds a verdict for the deficient designs that have rows enough, and the
sampler does not reliably cover that gap: of the 1200 such fits,
943 met every diagnostic. All 258
fits that failed a diagnostic belong to the deficient group, and every one of
them is binomial or Poisson. A clean set of diagnostics is not evidence that
the design is identified; compute the geometry from the aggregate table
before fitting.

## What this vignette does not claim

There is no universal minimum number of rows beyond $K + 1$, no validated
`cond_inv` cutoff, and no guarantee that an unflagged design gives a precise
target effect. The simulation uses synthetic strata, six designs, three
covariates, one effect size and no survival family; what it establishes is
the inversion, for which one counterexample is enough. A threshold for a
specific application would need that application's within-stratum
distributions, effect size, sample sizes and outcome family.
